description: Price a swap against one position, on-chain, at the current block — no custody, nothing signed, nothing moved. Works on any pair the position trades, not only stablecoins. Use this to check liquidity and get the output amount before preparing a swap. If a position answers "Strategy is gated", the maker embedded an access-licence check in the order: the CALLER must hold the 1inch Aqua access token. That check reads tx.origin, so the revert depends on whether a caller was supplied: without one it is 0x89c62b64 ("the caller holds none"), with one it is 0x39c4052c (the tx-origin balance check). Pass `from` with the address that will actually sign the swap. A caller that holds the maker's credential gets a real price; anyone else gets an accurate "you do not hold it" instead of the least specific answer available. This is a property of the strategy, not a bug — and it is strongly per-network. Measured 2026-10-19: on Ethereum 58 of 60 sampled positions are gated, and across 17 networks the network-balanced split is about 62 percent gated and 17 percent priced. The credential contract itself is only deployed on the 13 Aqua chains, so Arc, Monad, Cronos and HyperEVM have no such gate. The response also decodes the fee from the signed order: `fee_decoding` is decoded/none/unsupported, `maker_fee_percent` is the maker commission (for example 0.00025), `maker_fee_receiver` is its receiver, and `fees` lists every fee instruction. Quotes are simulated on 17 networks: ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, arc, bnb-chain, gnosis, avalanche, sonic, linea, zksync-era, monad, unichain, hyperevm, cronos and robinhood-chain. This list is the set the quote path actually serves; if a network is not on it, do not promise a quote for it.

amount.description: Input amount in token base units, as an integer string. e.g. "1000000" for 1 USDC.

from.description: The address that will sign the swap, simulated as msg.sender. Supply it whenever the caller might hold the maker's access credential: the gate is checked on tx.origin, so with an address the answer is the real one, and without one it is the least specific one.
